At 1st level, and at every even level thereafter, a fighter gains a bonus feat in addition to those gained from normal advancement (meaning that the fighter gains a feat at every level). These bonus feats must be selected from those listed as Combat Feats, sometimes also called "fighter bonus feats."

Upon reaching 4th level, and every four levels thereafter (8th, 12th, and so on), a fighter can choose to learn a new bonus feat in place of a bonus feat he has already learned. In effect, the fighter loses the bonus feat in exchange for the new one. The old feat cannot be one that was used as a prerequisite for another feat, prestige class, or other ability. A fighter can only change one feat at any given level and must choose whether or not to swap the feat at the time he gains a new bonus feat for the level.

candidates.rationale: Complete CRB class feature (p. 55) compared with the PRD capture (coreRulebook/classes/fighter.html:380-381, identical apart from Foundry's capitalised "Combat Feats") and PCGen's Core Rulebook row (cr_abilities_class.lst:893). Granted at 1st level (PCGen :257; Foundry classAssociations level 1) and at every even level: S3's reviewed schedule gives the acquisition and its ten everythingpath/fighter-bonus-feats-N increments (2nd to 20th) one feat slot each, {kind: feat, count: 1, featTypes: ['Combat']} (scripts/catalog/pcgen/schedule-slots.ts, printed at fighter.html:380), and the increments take this assessment through attributionFrom. Foundry's bonusFeats change (1 + floor(@class.level / 2)) has no mapped target and contributes nothing, so the slots are not doubled. The Note states the feat retraining rule (4th, 8th, ... 20th), which stays prose; retraining and the slot-type warning stay outstanding calculations. Existing reviewed CRB notice covers it.

mechanicsReview.name: Bonus Feats (FGT)
mechanicsReview.descriptionText:
At 1st level, and at every even level thereafter, a fighter gains a bonus feat in addition to those gained from normal advancement (meaning that the fighter gains a feat at every level). These bonus feats must be selected from those listed as Combat Feats, sometimes also called "fighter bonus feats."

Upon reaching 4th level, and every four levels thereafter (8th, 12th, and so on), a fighter can choose to learn a new bonus feat in place of a bonus feat he has already learned. In effect, the fighter loses the bonus feat in exchange for the new one. The old feat cannot be one that was used as a prerequisite for another feat, prestige class, or other ability. A fighter can only change one feat at any given level and must choose whether or not to swap the feat at the time he gains a new bonus feat for the level.

classFeatureReview.scheduleRule: Bonus feats gained by fighter level = 1 + floor(level / 2): one at 1st and one more at every even level, 11 at 20th (PRD :380 and table :357-376; PCGen BONUS:ABILITYPOOL|Fighter Bonus Feat|FighterLvl/2+1 at :893). Each is one slot restricted to Combat feats: the acquisition at 1st and increments everythingpath/fighter-bonus-feats-2 to -20.

slotReview.attribution: Each increment has attributionFrom pf1/CV8BsY3ciUb9TA1Y and upstreamKey pf1/CV8BsY3ciUb9TA1Y, so it takes this assessment, holds and notices and is admitted exactly when Bonus Feats is (scripts/catalog/admission.ts, isAttributionOwner). No increment has an assessment of its own.
slotReview.foundryChange: Foundry's change {target: bonusFeats, formula: 1 + floor(@class.level / 2), type: untyped} has no mapped target; the importer keeps it as an unsupported `changes` field that contributes nothing (scripts/catalog/map.ts), so no second slot count exists.

prerequisiteReview.review: A class feature has no selection prerequisite; it is granted by Fighter level (classFeatureReview). The Combat restriction is the slot's featTypes, not a prerequisite.

proficiencyReview.review: No weapon or armor proficiency grant in this body (the Fighter's proficiencies are the class's own: classes-596.json).
